title: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief From Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief From Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Investment Allowance for Emissions Reduction
sections.summary: The Bill expands the renamed IA-ER scheme to cover greenhouse gas emission reduction investments and extends its validity to 31 December 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The enhancement of the "Investment Allowance for Energy Efficiency" scheme, which is now renamed "Investment Allowance for Emissions Reduction" ("IA-ER"), was announced at Budget 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The scheme currently supports companies in improving their energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This Bill expands the scope of support to also include investments in equipment that result in measurable and verifiable reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The scheme's validity period has also been extended from 31 March 2021 to 31 December 2026, to support companies adapting and transiting to a low-carbon economy.

sections.label: Minister powers and greenhouse gas definitions
sections.summary: Clause 2 lets the Minister vest functions or powers in a public body, while clauses 3 and 4 add greenhouse gas definitions to tax incentive schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The bulk of the amendments concerns two elements: clause 2 inserts a new section that will allow the Minister to vest, unto a public body, functions or powers afforded by the Act to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 3 and 4, then introduce new definitions of greenhouse gas into the Act's tax incentive schemes, which aligns with this Government's Green Plan as well as the amendments to the Environmental Protection and Management Act, passed last year in this House.

sections.label: Financing incentives beyond tax breaks
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Government plans to continue financing economic incentives for firms adopting environmentally sustainable initiatives beyond tax breaks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the context of moving beyond tax breaks, I, therefore, wish to ask how the Government plans to continue its financing of economic incentives for firms that adopt environmentally sustainable initiatives.

sections.label: Elected representatives and delegation conditions
sections.summary: The Member argues elected representatives should decide inequality and tax matters, and asks what conditions and mechanisms govern delegation to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Here, my argument is that it should fall on elected representatives to determine how much inequality society can tolerate, which redistributive goals would be fair and just, and what types of taxes we should accommodate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Turning back to the Bill in question, I am left to wonder whether there are specific conditions that should be fulfilled, such as when the matter is explicitly technical in nature and when normative decision-making would not be asked for or required before the Minister would then allow for such delegation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And what mechanisms are there in place to ensure that both de facto as well as de jure ownership of decisions remain with the respective Minister?

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Allow me to clarify that these amendments would affect the applications for the investment allowance for emission reductions (IA-ER) that are received between 1 April 2021 and the time that the legislative amendments are passed.

sections.label: Backdating amendments to 1 April 2021
sections.summary: The amendments are backdated to 1 April 2021, the previously announced start date of the IA-ER.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In this instance, the amendments are being backdated to 1 April 2021, which was the previously announced start date of the IA-ER.

sections.label: Other energy and sustainability incentives
sections.summary: The Member recaps other incentives: the Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy, Energy Efficiency Fund, $180 million Enterprise Sustainability Programme, and Low-carbon Energy Research Funding initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Other incentives and schemes include ─ and I think some Members would have read about it, but allow me to recap ─ the Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy, the Energy Efficiency Fund, the $180 million Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) that was mentioned by Mr Don Wee, launched by ESG on 1 October last year, and the Low-carbon Energy Research Funding initiative.
